connection: Methods now organize behavior. This session introduces classes as definitions for objects that keep related state and rules together.
objectives: Distinguish a class definition from an object instance.
Use a constructor to establish required state.
Read properties as named parts of an object's public state.
Create separate objects whose values remain independent.

visuals.title: A class defines a shape
visuals.explanation: The class describes available construction, state, and behavior; each new expression creates a distinct instance.

visuals.title: Construction establishes required state
visuals.explanation: Constructor arguments enter validation and become property values only when the object can be created validly.

visuals.title: Properties expose named state
visuals.explanation: Properties let callers read meaningful state without exposing storage details as public fields.

visuals.title: Instances keep independent values
visuals.explanation: Two Worker objects follow the same class definition but can contain different identifiers and names.

preQuiz.explanation: new invokes the constructor and produces a reference to the created object.

preQuiz.prompt: Why require id and displayName in the constructor?
options: Every object starts with required state
preQuiz.explanation: Construction prevents a Worker from existing without its required identity.

preQuiz.prompt: If two Worker objects have different names, changing the variable that refers to one automatically changes the other?
preQuiz.explanation: They are separate instances with independent property values.

concept.title: Classes define; objects exist
paragraphs: Worker is a class: a reusable definition. worker is a variable whose value refers to one Worker object.
Keeping that vocabulary precise prevents confusion between changing a definition and creating an instance.

concept.title: Constructors establish invariants
paragraphs: The constructor checks required inputs before assigning properties. If validation fails, no usable Worker object is returned.
This concentrates creation rules at the boundary where state first enters the object.

concept.title: Properties communicate intent
paragraphs: Id and DisplayName are get-only properties. Callers can read them, while only construction assigns them.
The app uses worker.Id to create a TimeEntry and worker.DisplayName for human-readable output.

lab.objective: Create a Worker class and use one object in the TimeLedger workflow.
lab.startingCondition: Program.cs passes a raw worker identifier directly to TimeEntry.
steps: Add a constructor requiring id and displayName and validate blank values.
Expose get-only Id and DisplayName properties.
Create a Worker object in Program.cs and pass worker.Id to TimeEntry.
Display the worker name and identifier, then add constructor tests.
lab.expectedBehavior: The app displays Avery Chen (worker-001), and the expanded test suite passes.
lab.validation: dotnet build TimeLedger.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test TimeLedger.sln --configuration Release && dotnet run --project src/TimeLedger.App/TimeLedger.App.csproj --configuration Release --no-build

expectedFiles.why: Define worker state and construction rules.
Create and use a Worker object.

commit: session-05: teach classes objects properties and constructors
review: Required values enter through the constructor.
Validation messages name the invalid input.
Application output and tests match the lesson.

postQuiz.prompt: Why does Program pass worker.Id to TimeEntry?
options: TimeEntry currently stores a string identifier
postQuiz.explanation: The current TimeEntry contract accepts the identifier string.

postQuiz.prompt: What breaks if DisplayName assignment is removed from the constructor?
options: Nullable analysis/build reports uninitialized required state
postQuiz.explanation: A non-nullable get-only property must be initialized during construction.

postQuiz.prompt: What do the Worker tests prove?
options: Required properties and rejection of blank inputs
postQuiz.explanation: Tests provide focused evidence for the documented construction rules.

reflections: What belongs inside Worker rather than Program?
Why are get-only properties useful here?
How is an object different from the variable that refers to it?
whatBreaks: Removing Worker returns Program to disconnected primitive values. Removing constructor validation permits invalid identity state. Removing get accessors prevents callers from reading the values needed to create entries and display output.
summary: A class defines construction, state, and behavior. A constructor establishes required state, properties expose meaningful values, and each object is a distinct instance.
